thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: p99 tail latency spike detected for router cluster eu-west-bridge-3. p99 crossed SLO (target 500ms -> observed 2.4s). Streaming stall rate up ~0.9% (baseline 0.03%). Possible misrouting/egress hot partitioning. Auto-page triggered. thread_ts=5461122334

sanjay (oncall): ack. joining bridge now. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/router-tail. starting triage: check routing-policy rollouts and hotkeys.

amanda: grabbing recent router logs + top shards. query: `select shard_id, count(*) as q, p99_latency from router_metrics where cluster='eu-west-bridge-3' and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' group by shard_id order by q desc limit 10;`

amanda: results paste:```
shard-790: q=124k, p99=2.9s
shard-1024: q=98k, p99=2.1s
shard-7: q=4k, p99=540ms
```
these two shards are enormous compared to normal. looks like routing policy put hot traffic onto the same egress group.

ingress-bot: recent policy rollout: `rb-across-region-v2` deployed 2m ago by ryan. rollout config: prefer-local=false, ejection-weight=0.8 -> 0.95 for small shards. diff:```
- prefer-local: true
+ prefer-local: false
- ejection-weight: 0.5
+ ejection-weight: 0.95
```
this change increases cross-zone fanout and seems to concentrate hotkey flows on bridge-3 due to seed hashing skew.

ryan: that was my rollout. I see the diff. I pushed the emergency flag in to reduce prefer-local because we were seeing cold hotspots earlier. didn't anticipate the seed/hash interaction with hotkey grouping.

maria: customer-impact check: running counts for streaming requests that hit p99 > 1s in last 15m. `select count(distinct customer_id) from request_trace where cluster='eu-west-bridge-3' and latency > 1s and ts > now() - interval '15 minutes';`

maria: number = 13 customers (approx 0.04% of active customers this window). top impacted customer ids: cust_112, cust_998, cust_44. no errors in payloads, but perceived slowness for streaming/video-transcribe pipelines.

sanjay (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) roll back `rb-across-region-v2` to previous config (prefer-local=true) 2) temporarily increase egress pool for eu-west-bridge-3 to spread shards 3) enable eager-fallback to smaller model variant for streaming requests to reduce token-processing time. executing step 1 now: `POST /config/rollout/rollback rb-across-region-v2`

sanjay (oncall): rollback command returned 200. publishing to config: `cfg-commit-5461122350`

ingress-bot: detected config commit cfg-commit-5461122350 applied to clusters [eu-west-1, eu-west-2] at 5461122380. routing table reconciliation started.

amanda: watching metrics: p99 for shard-790 dropped to 1.6s -> 880ms in 90s after rollback. overall cluster p99 from 2.4s -> 720ms. streaming stalls down to 0.25%. still above target but trending down.

ryan: while rollback helped, seed/hash mapping still leaves shard-790 concentrated. temp mitigation: issue a soft-drain on hot shard and redispatch heavy keys using hashing fudge. running `curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/drain -d '{"shard":"shard-790","duration":600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`

ops-infra: approved temporary egress scale-up and permitted drain. egress pool scale command: `scale egress eu-west-bridge-3 --instances +4`. executing now.

ops-infra: scale returned success; new egress workers online in ~45s.

amanda: metrics update: p99 now 480ms for most shards; shard-790 p99 at 610ms after drain + scale. streaming stalls ~0.07%. SLO for p99 is back under 500ms for majority routes but some heavy-key tails at ~600ms.

maria: quick customer note drafted for customer ops: "We observed elevated latency affecting a small subset of customers in eu-west region. We rolled back a routing policy and scaled egress to restore SLOs. If you saw slow streaming, please DM infra@redwood and reference incident 5461122334." happy to ping the three impacted customers.

ryan: root-cause hypothesis: `rb-across-region-v2` inadvertently combined two changes: disabling prefer-local and bumping ejection-weight high. combination + current consistent hashing seeds resulted in hotkey concentration on bridge-3. We'll add a canary gate and a canary-seed shuffle for future rollouts.

sanjay (oncall): handing off to lee (next oncall) at 5461122899. summary for handoff: incident id 5461122334, initial p99=2.4s, rollback applied -> commit cfg-commit-5461122350, egress scaled +4, drain applied on shard-790, current cluster p99 ~480ms, customers impacted ~13. artifacts: runbook link, logs (https://logs.redwood/5461122334), replay traces (https://traces.redwood/5461122334). action items: 1) revert change to ejection-weight in rollout PR until canary tests 2) implement seed-randomization for rollouts 3) postmortem and customer comms (owner: ryan).

lee (oncall-next): joining. thanks for the handoff. I'll keep an eye for the next 2 hours and own postmortem notes. adding reaction :thumbsup: to the rollback and scale ops.

ops-infra: putting a 24h monitor alert for rb-across-region-v2 toggles and adding a gate to block ejection-weight > 0.8 until we validate.

amanda: copied logs and a condensed timeline to incident board. will attach a minimal repro (simulation that shows hotkey concentration given seed and policy).

maria: marking customer comms draft as pending and will send once postmortem has owner-approved text.

sanjay (oncall): closing bridge, switching to watch mode. good triage team. :coffee:

incidents-bot: incident 5461122334 status -> mitigated (SLOs recovering). paging cleared.
